newsitem.title: USA: Michigan officials confirm 150 hepatitis cases.
newsitem.headline: Michigan officials confirm 150 hepatitis cases.

text.p: About 150 students and teachers in central and southwest Michigan were confirmed to have contracted the hepatitis A virus after eating frozen sliced strawberries, state health officials said Wednesday.

Officials said 28 Michigan counties received the frozen strawberries, which originated from Mexico and were first shipped to the state Dec. 9, 1996, said Phil Kirkwood, head of the state's Food Safety Programme.
Those who were served the berries include 1,200 to 1,400 participants in a Special Olympics event held March 22 in Grand Rapids, Michigan.

Dr. David Johnson, chief medical executive of the Michigan Department of Community Health, said health agencies throughout the state have given thousands of injections of immune globulin, which is not a vaccine but contains antibodies to help prevent the illness. However, the effectiveness of the globulin goes away after about 14 days.
"It's quite clear that the contamination did not appear at any particular school building. It occurred somewhere upstream," Johnson said.

The berries were distributed to a total of six states as part of a U.S. Department of Agriculture-sponsored school meals programme by the San Diego firm of Anderson & Williams, a unit of Epitope Inc, based in Beaverton, Ore.
